paragraph: Teterboro recorded no closings in any tier over the last six months, single-family, multi-family, condo, or co-op. That isn't a soft market, it's an absence of one. With zero sales there's no median, no sale-to-list ratio, and no days on market to read, and no monthly series to place against the usual Bergen County arc where medians build into early summer and closing volume bottoms out in deep winter. The residential inventory here is small enough that entire six-month windows pass without a transaction, so when something does list, it sets its own comparables rather than following a local pattern. If you're set on Teterboro, the practical move is a standing alert and a pricing read built from neighboring Bergen County towns, because you won't get one from activity inside the borough itself.
